items.headline: Gaborik, five days in, says Toronto's room is not the one people picture
items.dek: After a quiet night in a 4-0 win, the newest Leaf says the room is younger than its reputation.

items.headline: The Long Way Round: Teemu Selanne's road to Colorado
items.dek: He taught kindergarten in Espoo, served in the Finnish army, and signed an offer sheet Calgary couldn't hold. At 34, he's on the best team in the league with one year left.

items.headline: First Overall, Last Place: Ilya Kovalchuk plays for July
items.dek: A 137-point pace on a 14-point team, with one year left at $1.10M

items.headline: Dollar-per-Point: The Expiring Class, Ranked
items.dek: The league's 24- and 25-year-old stars are producing at $20K a point. The veterans they'll replace next summer cost three times that.

items.headline: League-best offense meets East-best defense when the Devils visit the Air Canada Centre
items.dek: Toronto scores 5.8 a night. New Jersey allows 2.9. Both streaks are live, and tonight one of them ends.

items.headline: LEAFS 4, NYI 0: Aebischer blanks the Islanders for the 11th straight, and New Jersey visits tonight
items.dek: The shutout over New York was the second in a row. The 14-2-3 Devils bring the road record of the century into the Air Canada Centre on Monday.

items.headline: DANFORTH: Gaborik reads 95 on the Index and costs $1.10M, and I have been staring at both numbers since Saturday
items.dek: The Bureau has him up 6 on the Development Index. He has 20 goals in 26 games. His contract expires in July. None of those three facts can survive the other two.

items.headline: DANFORTH: $6.50M buys 10 starts and a folding chair, and I have made peace with hating it
items.dek: I still trust Belfour more than anyone else in this crease. I also know what his contract costs the team that will not play him.

items.headline: The Index Went Up at Los Angeles While Everything Else Stayed the Same
items.dek: Three under-23s, three of the league's biggest jumps on the Development Index, and a team buried last in the Pacific at 23 points

items.headline: THE COACH SAT WHOM: Five benches, five better men, zero excuses
items.dek: The grading says who's better. The lineup card says the coach doesn't care. Here are five clubs paying for it.

items.headline: $78 TO WATCH CLIFF RONNING PLAY 8.8 MINUTES: PHILADELPHIA IS THE NEW MOST OVERPAID MESS
items.dek: $69.07 million buys $2.76 million per point, four straight losses, and two men collecting $2.77M and $2.10M for under 10 minutes a night.

items.headline: RUMOR METER: Vancouver's Blue Line Just Collapsed. They Have to Buy. 🔥🔥
items.dek: Two defensemen signed within 24 hours, both on the shelf. The cheapest club in the league is now forced to shop.

items.headline: RUMOR METER: 12 Deals Signed This Week. 6 Players Injured. Same 4-Day Window. 🔥🔥
items.dek: Every IR onset in the signing class falls between Dec. 4 and Dec. 7. Two of them re-signed at pay cuts that smell like a medical caveat.

items.headline: RECAP: Tampa Bay 7, Edmonton 1 -- a 29-shot night and 41 goals in 10
items.dek: The Lightning's 7-1 over the Oilers keeps a 7-3 run alive and puts them 3 points behind Carolina.

items.headline: Goalie Watch: Islanders pull DiPietro after a 4-0 loss; Snow starts in Pittsburgh
items.dek: Three netminders, one crease, and a team that scored zero on 13 shots.

items.headline: The Blaine Rankings, Week 3: Peter Forsberg is the Hart frontrunner, and his club is 12-1 on the road
items.dek: Three players share a 173-point pace, the oldest of them leads in points, and the one whose team will let him keep the trophy plays in Colorado.

items.headline: The Mis-Slotted Eight: Where the Book Says Ice Time Is Going to the Wrong Player
items.dek: Rostislav Klesla grades 82 and plays the third pair. Carlo Colaiacovo grades 71 and plays five slots. The 11-point gap is the league's widest, but it isn't the only one.

items.headline: Goalie Timeshares League-Wide: True No. 1s vs. Committees
items.dek: Twenty-eight clubs have a starter. Only two do not — and one of them is spending $67 million to split work between a 92 and an 85.

items.headline: What the Book Never Said: Toronto's young men, all arriving at once
items.dek: 4 under-23s on the Index risers in the same fortnight, 11 straight wins, and a goal differential that makes the rest of the league look like a different sport.

items.headline: At 34, leading the league: who Bill Guerin has become
items.dek: Fifty-eight points in twenty-seven games, a 176 pace, and a Dallas club built around the oldest men in the room.

items.headline: Young Guns Watch: 4 Leafs on the Index risers, and I cannot find a reason to be smug about any of them
items.dek: The Development Index has more Toronto players climbing than any other club. The streak is not luck. That is the problem.

items.headline: THE PANIC METER: code Green for the first time I can remember, and I hate how it feels
items.dek: Ten straight, Gaborik is the best player in the league, McCabe is putting up numbers no defenseman should. So why can't I stop looking at Brad Richards?

items.headline: Injury Desk: Belfour returns tomorrow, and Aebischer has no reason to give the crease back
items.dek: The 39-year-old is back from a 3-day absence. The 26-year-old has 13 starts and a 10-game winning streak.

items.headline: Goalie Room: Belfour back tomorrow, but Aebischer owns the crease now
items.dek: The 39-year-old returns from a 2004-12-05 injury with a $6.50M cap hit and a 92 overall. The 26-year-old behind him has 13 starts, a 10-game winning streak, and zero reasons to give his job back.

items.headline: DANFORTH: Brad Richards is the answer, and that is what terrifies me
items.dek: The second-centre problem I have written about every day since October might be solved, and nobody on this roster looks like they want to talk about what happens in July.

items.headline: DANFORTH: 10 straight wins and the only number I care about is $1.00M
items.dek: Brad Richards is outplaying his contract by every measure on the sheet, and it expires in July.

items.headline: The Toronto Ascension: six under-23s, all rising, all on the same page
items.dek: No other team in the league has more than 2 players under 23 with positive form on the Development Index right now. Toronto has 6.

items.headline: The Pick in the Basement: How Toronto Got Detroit's First Without Lifting a Finger
items.dek: The Lions are 5 straight losses from the bottom of the standings, and the map on that first-rounder leads right to Toronto's war room

items.headline: I Saw Him When: Petr Chlup and the 18-year-old running Toronto
items.dek: The youngest player on the Book's U-23 board is already a difference-maker on the league's best team — and the rest of that team's youth wave makes this look like a dynasty in embryo.

items.headline: WHAT $80.89 MILLION BUYS YOU: A 40-YEAR-OLD AND A MAN WHO PLAYS NINE MINUTES
items.dek: Last week I told you Detroit was the most overpaid team in hockey. Here's the autopsy. The roster isn't just expensive. It's badly built, and the coach is holding the chisel.

items.headline: THE MOST OVERPAID TEAM IN HOCKEY (DO THE MATH)
items.dek: Detroit spends $80.89 million to buy 26 points and a five-game skid. Vancouver spends half that and has more wins than Detroit has losses.

items.headline: HOT SEAT METER: FIVE COACHES POLISHING THE RÉSUMÉ
items.dek: Losing streaks, buried paychecks, and goalies who can't look at you. The blame sheet says these 5 benches are about to get uncomfortable.

items.headline: Sources: Morale Problems Brewing in Minnesota
items.dek: The four unhappiest players in the league all have expiring contracts. Two of them are goalies for the worst team in the Northwest.

items.headline: RUMOR METER: Fire Sale Brewing in Atlanta? 🔥🔥
items.dek: The league's worst team has two 20-something superstars on expiring pennies. The phone is about to ring off the hook.

items.headline: Contract-Year Watch: 5 Expiring Deals and the Best Record in the League. Only One Club Has Both.
items.dek: No other contender has more than 2 high-end contracts walking at season's end. Toronto has 5, and the Maple Leafs are 18-5-0.

items.headline: Numbers Game: Colorado has 42 points without Sakic or Kariya
items.dek: The Avalanche are 20-4-0 with the league's best road record and two 84-overall forwards out

items.headline: Goalie Watch: Two creases, one question — who starts when the numbers don't lie?
items.dek: Toronto's 10-game heater has been built on suffocating defence, while New Jersey just sat down its all-time wins leader. Both netminders face a Saturday reckoning.

items.headline: Goalie Watch: New Jersey benches Brodeur after 20 starts in 22 games
items.dek: Ari Ahonen moves into the crease for the league's lowest goals-against total

items.headline: Goalie Watch: Belfour returns to a crease that kept winning without him
items.dek: Toronto's 10-game streak produced 18 goals against. Two netminders share the credit. Only one can start Saturday.

items.headline: The Blaine Rankings, Week 2: The gap between the elite and the field is now measured in goals, not points
items.dek: Toronto's +57 in ten games is not a points total that can be chased. It is a statement about what these two clubs are and what everyone else is not.

items.headline: The Blaine Rankings, Week 1: Two clubs have left the field, and one of them is tearing through it
items.dek: Toronto's ten-game winning streak has produced a goal differential no other club has matched all season, while Colorado sits one point ahead with a steadier hand. Everyone else is negotiating for relevance.

items.headline: Award Watch: the Vezina is Brodeur's to lose, and the Devils are the third team nobody ranked
items.dek: New Jersey's points-per-game pace is the best in the league, their cost-per-point is the cheapest, and Martin Brodeur's numbers are ahead of everyone who has played enough games to qualify.
